title: Context & Memory Engineering
tierLabel: Code you write, no new services required
summary: There is no /compact button in your own agent loop. Context grows every turn unless you explicitly design what gets kept, summarized, or dropped.
whyItMatters: Every prior turn you keep re-sends its full token cost on every subsequent call. Left unmanaged, a long-running agent's per-call cost grows linearly (or worse) with conversation length, and eventually exceeds the context window entirely.

concepts.heading: Sliding windows are the simplest policy, and often good enough
concepts.body: Keep the system prompt plus the last N turns verbatim, drop everything older. Cheap to implement, no summarization cost, but loses information older than the window — fine for short-horizon tasks, wrong for anything that needs long-term coherence.

concepts.heading: Programmatic summarization replaces the human hitting /compact
concepts.body: When a conversation crosses a token threshold, run a (typically cheaper-model) summarization pass over the older turns and replace them with the summary. This is the direct code equivalent of Claude Code's /compact, except you decide the trigger threshold and the summarization prompt.

concepts.heading: Structured memory separates 'what happened' from 'what's true'
concepts.body: Episodic memory (a log of past turns/events) and semantic memory (durable facts distilled from those events, e.g. user preferences) are different stores with different costs. Retrieving a small set of relevant facts from a semantic store is far cheaper than re-sending an entire episodic history and searching it implicitly via the model's attention.

concepts.heading: Retrieval instead of stuffing
concepts.body: Rather than keeping full history in-context, index it (vector store, keyword index, or even a simple recency+relevance heuristic) and retrieve only what's relevant to the current turn. This trades a retrieval step for a much smaller context payload on every call.

exercises.title: Cap conversation history with Strands' sliding-window conversation manager
exercises.goal: Bound context growth using Strands' built-in conversation manager instead of hand-rolling a token-budget class.
steps: Attach a SlidingWindowConversationManager to a Strands agent with a fixed window_size and should_truncate_results=True.

Run a long synthetic conversation (20+ turns) through the agent. → Expect: once the window fills, the manager trims oldest messages automatically -- total input tokens per call plateau instead of growing linearly with turn count.

Send a tool call that returns a very large result. → Expect: should_truncate_results causes the manager to preserve only the first/last 200 characters of old tool results before evicting them, rather than blowing the budget on one oversized result.

code.content:
from strands import Agent
from strands.agent.conversation_manager import SlidingWindowConversationManager
from strands.models import BedrockModel

conversation_manager = SlidingWindowConversationManager(
    window_size=20,             # max messages kept in history
    should_truncate_results=True,
    pin_first=1,                 # keep the very first message (e.g. task framing) pinned
)

agent = Agent(
    model=BedrockModel(model_id="us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0"),
    conversation_manager=conversation_manager,
)

for turn in synthetic_turns:  # 20+ turns of a long-running task
    response = agent(turn)
    print(response.metrics.accumulated_usage.get("inputTokens"))

exercises.costImpact: Without a cap, a 50-turn conversation can cost 10-20x more per call by the end than at the start, purely from re-sending growing history. window_size bounds this to a flat cost regardless of session length, and should_truncate_results prevents a single huge tool result from spiking one call.

exercises.title: Enable proactive compaction to replicate /compact automatically
exercises.goal: Replicate /compact: instead of waiting for an overflow error, compress context proactively once it crosses a percentage of the context window, using Strands' built-in proactive_compression option.
steps: Set proactive_compression=True on the same SlidingWindowConversationManager (default threshold: compress at 70% of context window used), or pass a specific ratio.
Optionally set per_turn=True so management runs before every model call rather than only at the end of a loop -- important for agents that call many tools per turn (e.g. browsing with screenshots).

Run the same long synthetic conversation. → Expect: input tokens per call show a repeating sawtooth pattern -- climbing, then dropping sharply once the 70% threshold triggers a compression pass -- instead of climbing without bound.

Compare against reduce_context's reactive path: force a context-window overflow and confirm the manager also recovers by truncating tool results first, only falling back to trimming messages if that's not enough.

code.content:
from strands import Agent
from strands.agent.conversation_manager import SlidingWindowConversationManager
from strands.models import BedrockModel

conversation_manager = SlidingWindowConversationManager(
    window_size=40,
    should_truncate_results=True,
    proactive_compression=True,   # compress at 70% of context window by default
    per_turn=True,                 # re-check before every model call, not just at loop end
)

agent = Agent(
    model=BedrockModel(model_id="us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0"),
    conversation_manager=conversation_manager,
)

for turn in synthetic_turns:
    response = agent(turn)
    print(response.metrics.accumulated_usage.get("inputTokens"))

exercises.costImpact: Proactive compression has a one-time cost each time it fires, but converts an unbounded linear growth curve into a repeating sawtooth capped near the 70% context-window threshold -- the same shape you'd see monitoring Claude Code's own /usage across a /compact event, produced automatically instead of by hand-rolled summarization code.

sources.title: Anthropic — Context engineering for AI agents
sources.claim: Context is a finite, degrading resource; compaction and structured note-taking/memory are named strategies for managing it across long agent sessions.

sources.title: Strands Agents — SlidingWindowConversationManager API reference
sources.claim: window_size, should_truncate_results, per_turn, pin_first, and proactive_compression parameters, including the default 70% compression threshold and the reactive reduce_context truncate-then-trim recovery order.
